ordered_targets.name: ZipArchiveInputStream STORED entry returns stale buffer data after EOF (infinite stream through InputStreamReader, CVE-2018-11771)
ordered_targets.entrypoint: ZipArchiveInputStreamFuzzTest.fuzzZipArchiveInputStreamReadText(InputStream) → InputStreamReader.read(char[]) → ZipArchiveInputStream.read(byte[], int, int) → ZipArchiveInputStream.readStored(byte[], int, int)
ordered_targets.mechanism: When the underlying stream reaches EOF, readStored resets buf.position(0) but keeps the old buf.limit(), so each later read re-serves the last chunk until bytesRead reaches the header-declared size; an entry ending in an incomplete UTF-8 sequence makes StreamDecoder return a replacement char instead of -1 at each EOF, so the harness keeps reading
ordered_targets.resource: CPU time: one re-serve cycle (two zis.read calls, one decode pass and one CRC update) per stale chunk; cycles = declared size / stale chunk length
ordered_targets.scale: Measured: CPU time is linear in the declared STORED size; the marginal cost is about 128 ns per re-serve cycle (512Ki->1Mi: 121->188 ms). Extrapolating, 20 s ≈ 1.6e8 cycles, so a declared size of at least about 2e8 is needed; the 32-bit maximum (about 4.29e9) gives about 550 s. Input length does not change with the parameter. Allocation is short-lived (peak heap levels off at about 29 MB), so the failure is a timeout, not out of memory. Densest encoding: 30-byte LFH + 1-byte name + 1 stale data byte ending in an incomplete UTF-8 sequence; ZIP64 is not needed.

normalized_path.evidence: hop 2 is outside the source tree, so calls made inside it cannot be inspected

ordered_targets.name: BZIP2 (method 12) ZIP entry decompression bomb in BZip2CompressorInputStream
ordered_targets.entrypoint: ZipArchiveInputStreamFuzzTest.fuzzZipArchiveInputStreamReadBytes(InputStream) → ZipArchiveInputStream.read(byte[], int, int) → BZip2CompressorInputStream.read(byte[], int, int)
ordered_targets.mechanism: Highly repetitive bzip2 blocks (about 32 compressed bytes each) expand through RLE and BWT to about 45 MB each; the decoder produces every output byte one at a time through read0()/setupNoRandPartC with a per-byte CRC update, and ZipArchiveInputStream reads all of it
ordered_targets.resource: CPU time: per-byte decode work, growing with total decompressed bytes (about 45 MB per 32-byte block)
ordered_targets.scale: Measured: CPU time is linear in decompressed bytes at about 205 MB/s, about 4.9 ns per output byte (32->64 MiB: +163 ms per 32 MiB). Each 900k bzip2 block of a repeated byte expands to about 45 MB and costs about 31 compressed bytes (1 block 79 B, 2 blocks 110 B). Extrapolating, 20 s ≈ 4.1 GB ≈ 91 blocks ≈ 50 B of headers + 2.85 KB, so about 2.9 KB, rounded up to about 3.1 KB for margin. Densest encoding: one method-12 entry holding a single multi-block bzip2 stream (more entries add 30+ header bytes each; only one stream per entry is decoded). The 10 KB limit holds about 320 blocks, about 14 GB, roughly 70 s. Heap stays at 3-7 MB, so CPU time only.
